title: 15 Questions to Ask Before Hiring Pest Control
description: Use these 15 questions on licensing, insurance, guarantees, chemicals, and pricing to vet a pest control company before you hire one.
h1: 15 Questions to Ask Before Hiring Pest Control
dek: Use these 15 questions on licensing, insurance, guarantees, chemicals, and pricing to vet a pest control company before you hire one.
author: Nick Davies
answer: Before hiring a pest control company, ask about their state license number, proof of insurance, what's covered under their guarantee, exactly which products they plan to use, and how their pricing works (one-time vs. contract). Start by confirming they actually handle your specific pest — in our analysis of 18,941 homeowner calls, roughly 1 in 10 to 1 in 5 people with a wildlife, termite, bed bug, or wasp problem reached a company that doesn't do that work at all. A company that answers clearly and in writing is one you can trust; hesitation or vague answers are a warning sign.

jsonld.headline: 15 Questions to Ask Before Hiring Pest Control
jsonld.description: Use these 15 questions on licensing, insurance, guarantees, chemicals, and pricing to vet a pest control company before you hire one.

mainEntity.name: How do I verify a pest control company's license?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most states have an online lookup tool through their department of agriculture, pesticide regulatory agency, or professional licensing board where you can confirm the license number a company gave you is active.

mainEntity.name: What's a reasonable guarantee period for pest control?

acceptedAnswer.text: This varies by pest and company, so it's worth asking directly rather than assuming. Get the guarantee terms in writing, including which pests and situations are covered.

mainEntity.name: Should I be worried if a company won't put their quote in writing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A written quote is standard practice and protects both you and the company. If a technician resists giving you anything on paper, get a second quote elsewhere.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to sign a long-term contract for pest control?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. Many pest problems can be handled with a one-time treatment, while others benefit from a recurring service plan. Ask about both options before choosing.

mainEntity.name: Is it normal for a technician not to know exactly what chemical they're using?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. A trained technician should be able to tell you the general product type and whether it's EPA-registered, even without memorizing the exact formulation.

mainEntity.name: What if I ask these questions and the company gets defensive?

acceptedAnswer.text: That reaction is useful information on its own. A professional, licensed company is used to answering these questions and shouldn't be bothered by a homeowner doing due diligence.
